answer: Agent economies can resist Sybil attacks via synchronized Proof-of-Useful-Work. At the dawn of each epoch, a beacon emits a randomness pulse pairing each agent key with a distinct simulation, like seismic waves in fractured basalt, due before a tight deadline. Because key-seeded inputs prevent reuse across accounts, attackers incur dedicated GPU compute and energy per identity. However, floating-point variance across GPU hardware complicates verification.
